Revenue comes from royalties and distributions from those partnerships. A B2B gas investment vehicle with no consumer brand. Gas is sold under long-term contracts, so returns depend on volumes and prices.

Beijing-based Chinese insurer offering property and casualty cover (motor, commercial and agricultural) and life and health insurance, with strong rural and car-insurance distribution through agents and brokers. It is listed in Hong Kong and has assets in the hundreds of billions of yuan. Recognised in China's insurance industry, but with moderate consumer brand awareness. It sells mostly to Chinese consumers and businesses through agents and brokers.

Canadian licensed cannabis producer, listed on the TSX and Nasdaq (ACB), selling medical and adult-use recreational cannabis in Canada, medical cannabis in Germany, Australia and other export markets. Brands include Aurora Drift, San Rafael '71, Daily Special and the medical MedReleaf and CanniMed lines, plus consumer products from Reliva and the pet range. Revenue is in the low hundreds of millions of Canadian dollars after a period of heavy write-downs and restructuring. Known in the cannabis industry, but marketing is restricted by law.

San Diego biopharmaceutical company (Nasdaq: ACAD) focused on neurology and rare disease. Its products are Nuplazid for hallucinations and delusions in Parkinson's disease psychosis and Daybue, approved in 2023 as the first drug for Rett syndrome. Revenue from sales is more than 500 million dollars a year, sold through specialty pharmacies to neurologists and psychiatrists in the US, with Europe expansion. Founded 1993. B2B and patient-focused healthcare brand with minimal general consumer awareness.

San Diego biopharmaceutical company (Nasdaq: ACAD) focused on neurology and rare disease. Its products are Nuplazid for hallucinations and delusions in Parkinson's disease psychosis and Daybue, approved in 2023 as the first drug for Rett syndrome. Revenue from sales is more than 500 million dollars a year, sold through specialty pharmacies to neurologists and psychiatrists in the US, with Europe expansion. Founded 1993. B2B and patient-focused healthcare brand with minimal general consumer awareness.

Cambridge, Massachusetts biopharmaceutical company (Nasdaq: AGIO) focused on cellular metabolism and rare blood disorders. Its marketed drug is Pyrukynd (mitapivat) for hemolytic anemia in pyruvate kinase deficiency, being studied in thalassemia and sickle cell disease. It sold its oncology business, including Tibsovo, to Servier in 2021 for around 1.8 billion dollars. Sells to haematologists through specialty distribution in the US and Europe. B2B healthcare, little general public brand awareness.

San Francisco gene therapy developer that built adeno-associated virus treatments for rare neuromuscular diseases, led by AT132 for X-linked myotubular myopathy and programmes in Pompe disease and other disorders. It operated its own gene therapy manufacturing in North Carolina and was listed on Nasdaq (BOLD). Astellas acquired it in early 2020 for roughly 3 billion dollars. Clinical-stage, no marketed products at the time, and no consumer profile.

Redwood City medical robotics company that developed the Monarch platform, a flexible robotic endoscopy system for bronchoscopy to reach early lung nodules and for urology procedures, sold to hospitals. Johnson & Johnson acquired it in 2019 in a deal worth up to 5.75 billion dollars, and it operates inside J&J MedTech's robotics business. Its customers are hospitals and physicians rather than the public, so it has low consumer awareness.

Cambridge, Massachusetts epigenetics-focused drug developer, whose lead candidate pelabresib (CPI-0610) was being developed for myelofibrosis, a rare blood cancer. It listed on Nasdaq (CNST) in 2018 and was acquired by German biotech MorphoSys in 2021 for about 1.7 billion dollars; MorphoSys was then bought by Novartis in 2024. Clinical-stage biotech, so B2B only with no consumer presence. Its pelabresib programme targeted bromodomain (BET) inhibition, and the deal was driven by the late-stage MANIFEST-2 data.

Cambridge, Massachusetts biopharmaceutical company (Nasdaq: EPZM) that developed Tazverik (tazemetostat), a first-in-class EZH2 inhibitor approved for epithelioid sarcoma and relapsed follicular lymphoma, sold to oncologists in the US. Revenue was modest, around 30 to 40 million dollars. Ipsen acquired Epizyme in 2022 for roughly 247 million dollars plus a contingent value right. Oncology specialist with no consumer awareness. Tazverik was the first approved drug in its class and was launched in 2020, but sales remained limited and the company relied on partners in Japan and Greater China.

New Jersey oncology biotech that developed Trodelvy (sacituzumab govitecan), an antibody-drug conjugate for triple-negative breast cancer and other solid tumours, approved by the FDA in 2020. It was listed on Nasdaq (IMMU). Gilead acquired it in October 2020 for roughly 21 billion dollars, and Trodelvy is now one of Gilead's growth drugs, with annual sales above 1 billion dollars. B2B pharma, no consumer awareness.

Animal nutrition company producing premixes, feed ingredients, additives and specialty feed for livestock and pets, serving farmers and feed manufacturers in more than 50 countries. It was owned by the French cooperative group InVivo and was acquired by Archer Daniels Midland (ADM) in 2019 for around 1.5 billion euros, becoming part of ADM Animal Nutrition. B2B agriculture supplier with no consumer brand visibility.

Medical device company focused on extremity orthopaedics (foot and ankle, shoulder, upper limb) and biologics, with products such as total ankle replacements and shoulder systems sold to hospitals and surgeons. Formed from Wright Medical Group and Tornier, with a Memphis operational base, and listed on Nasdaq (WMGI). Stryker acquired it in November 2020 for around 5.4 billion dollars. B2B med-tech, no general consumer visibility.

Cambridge, Massachusetts gene therapy company created in a spin-off from Switzerland-based Ferring Pharmaceuticals to commercialise nadofaragene firadenovec, sold as Adstiladrin, a gene therapy for BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer that the FDA approved in 2022. Customers are urologists and hospitals. Privately held and backed by Ferring and investors, so B2B with minimal public brand recognition. The bladder cancer market is large, with several hundred thousand patients living with the disease in the US, and the therapy is delivered by instillation into the bladder in the urologist's office.

Guobang Pharma is a Chinese company in Hangzhou, Zhejiang, focused on pharmaceutical research, development and manufacturing, according to the input. No product names, customers or scale can be confirmed. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Boston-area biotechnology company (Nasdaq: IRWD) whose main product is Linzess (linaclotide) for irritable bowel syndrome with constipation and chronic constipation, which it sells in the US with AbbVie and licensed to partners in Asia and Europe. It generates several hundred million dollars from royalties and profit share. Spun off Cyclerion in 2019 and founded in 1998. Linzess is widely advertised to consumers.

Chinese pharmacy chain operator based in Changsha, Hunan, running thousands of company-owned and franchised drugstores across many provinces, selling prescription and over-the-counter drugs, health products and offering online pharmacy services. Listed in Shanghai, it is among China's largest drugstore chains by store count. Brand recognition is strong among consumers in central and southern China. The company sells through its store network under the Laobaixing name and also runs wholesale and online channels, with an estimated annual revenue in the tens of billions of yuan.

Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company (Nasdaq: MACK) that developed Onivyde, a liposomal irinotecan for pancreatic cancer, which it sold to Ipsen in 2017, before shrinking and winding down its drug pipeline and operations. It was founded in 2000 around network biology. Today it has little or no operations, so there is no meaningful sponsorship or consumer profile. It returned cash to shareholders after the asset sale and kept only a small research pipeline.

Massachusetts medical device maker of proton therapy systems for cancer, notably the compact single-room Mevion S250 and S250i with HYPERSCAN pencil beam scanning, sold to hospitals and cancer centres in the US and abroad. Its systems are cheaper and smaller than conventional cyclotron installations. Privately held with institutional investors. B2B with little general consumer awareness. It was founded in 2004 as Still River Systems, a spin-off from MIT-linked research, and sells to US hospitals and cancer centres.

Redwood City biopharmaceutical company that developed Veltassa (patiromer), a potassium binder for hyperkalemia in patients with kidney and heart disease, sold to nephrologists and cardiologists. It listed on Nasdaq (RLYP) in 2013 and was acquired by Swiss company Galenica in 2016 for around 1.5 billion dollars, later part of Vifor Pharma and CSL. B2B healthcare, no consumer visibility. Veltassa sold through hospital pharmacies and retail channels, and annual revenues were in the low hundreds of millions of dollars after launch.

Biopharmaceutical company focused on cancer immunotherapy, developing PD-L1 antibody envafolimab (KN035) with Alphamab and other oncology candidates, with operations in China and a US presence. It sells to hospitals and oncologists, with licensing and regional commercial agreements. It is privately held with venture backing. Clinical-stage and early commercial, so B2B with no consumer awareness. Its US base in Fremont, California supports clinical trials and business development for Western markets, while commercial sales are driven mostly through Chinese partners.

California neurology-focused pharma company (Nasdaq: ADMS) that sold Gocovri (extended-release amantadine) for dyskinesia in Parkinson's disease and Osmolex ER, using proprietary controlled-release technology. Customers are neurologists in the US through specialty channels. Acquired in November 2021 by Supernus Pharmaceuticals for roughly 400 million dollars. B2B healthcare, no consumer brand awareness. Gocovri was the first drug approved specifically for dyskinesia in Parkinson's, and Adamas was founded in 2000 in the San Francisco Bay Area.

California biotech (Nasdaq: AIMT) that launched Palforzia, the first FDA-approved treatment for peanut allergy in children, based on controlled oral immunotherapy, sold through allergists. Nestlé Health Science acquired Aimmune in 2020 for around 2.6 billion dollars, and Palforzia now sits within Nestlé. Customers are allergists, hospitals and families with allergic children, so brand awareness is moderate in niche circles. Palforzia's launch in 2020 was hit by COVID-19 and slow patient uptake, but the product remained a first-in-class treatment, with peanut allergy affecting roughly 1-2% of children.

Waltham, Massachusetts clinical-stage biopharma that uses an AI and multi-omics platform built on patient biology to discover drugs and biomarkers, with candidates including BPM31510 for glioblastoma and pancreatic cancer. It grew out of Berg and works with academic and industry partners. Privately held and venture-backed, B2B with no consumer profile. Its approach combines patient tissue samples, mass spectrometry data and artificial intelligence to identify disease mechanisms, rather than one single product.

Cambridge, Massachusetts clinical-stage immuno-oncology company (Nasdaq: GNCA) developing neoantigen cancer vaccines (GEN-009) and checkpoint-related therapies, using a platform for identifying T-cell targets. It ran early clinical trials and had pharma partnerships, but struggled to fund development and went through bankruptcy and liquidation in 2022. B2B biotech with no consumer profile. Genocea was founded in 2007 in Cambridge and went public in 2014, with a platform called ATLAS used for identifying antigens from tumour samples.

Cambridge, Massachusetts oncology drug developer (Nasdaq: INFI) whose main product was Copiktra (duvelisib), a PI3K inhibitor for blood cancers licensed to Secura Bio, plus other PI3K-gamma candidates such as eganelisib. Revenues came from licensing and royalties, not product sales. It filed for Chapter 11 in 2023 as funding ran out. B2B biotech, no consumer visibility. Copiktra was approved in 2018 and commercialised by Verastem and later Secura Bio, with Infinity receiving milestones and royalties.

Flagship Pioneering company in Cambridge, Massachusetts developing therapeutics based on engineered circular RNA (eRNA), an RNA drug platform with long-lasting expression. It raised significant venture funding and was renamed Sail Biomedicines in 2022. Pre-clinical or early stage, so it works with research and pharma partners rather than consumers, and has no consumer awareness. Flagship incubated it in stealth and launched it publicly in 2021, making the circular RNA platform one of the better funded in biotech.

Los Angeles plant-based food holding company that assembled meat and dairy alternative brands, including Oumph!, Fry's Family Food, Like Meat and Wicked Kitchen, and sold them through retailers in Europe, North America and Asia. It also ran a media site on plant-based living. Sold through supermarkets and foodservice, and the portfolio was later restructured. Moderate brand awareness among plant-based consumers.

Palo Alto software company whose cloud platform runs decentralised clinical trials, remote patient data capture, electronic consent and AI-assisted trial tools for pharmaceutical companies, CROs and academic centres. It raised hundreds of millions of dollars, with a valuation above 2 billion dollars in 2021. Revenue comes from subscriptions and services. B2B, little awareness outside life sciences. Its tools cover patient apps, video visits and e-consent for people taking part in trials, rather than treating them, and have been used by large pharma sponsors.

Biopharmaceutical company that developed Orgovyx (relugolix) for advanced prostate cancer and Myfembree for uterine fibroids and endometriosis pain, selling to urologists and gynaecologists in the US. It was majority-owned by Sumitomo Pharma and listed on the NYSE (MYOV) before being taken fully into Sumitomo in 2023 for roughly 1.7 billion dollars. B2B, with patient-facing marketing for women's health. Myfembree was co-commercialised with Pfizer, and Orgovyx was the first oral GnRH antagonist for prostate cancer, offering an alternative to injections.

San Diego biotech (Nasdaq: OTIC) that developed drugs for ear disorders, including the marketed Otiprio antibiotic gel for middle ear infections and pipeline treatments for hearing loss and tinnitus. It sold to ear, nose and throat specialists in the US. After clinical setbacks it wound down and dissolved around 2023. No consumer visibility. Otonomy was founded in 2008 and listed on Nasdaq in 2014, and its pipeline included OTO-413 and OTO-313 for hearing loss and tinnitus, which did not succeed.

Irish neuroscience company (Nasdaq: PRTA), spun out of Elan, developing antibody immunotherapies against protein misfolding diseases, including birtamimab for AL amyloidosis and programmes in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's with partners such as Novo Nordisk and Roche. It receives collaboration and royalty revenue, with no marketed product of its own. B2B clinical-stage biotech, no consumer awareness. Prothena was formed in 2012 and operates from Dublin and South San Francisco, and its shares trade on Nasdaq with a market value in the low billions of dollars.

Beijing vaccine maker (Nasdaq: SVA) best known for CoronaVac, an inactivated COVID-19 vaccine used in China and shipped to dozens of countries such as Indonesia, Brazil and Turkey. Other products include hepatitis A (Healive), EV71 and varicella vaccines. Revenue peaked in 2021 and fell afterwards, with management disputes. Known through the pandemic to the public, but largely B2B government sales.

Chinese-founded clinical trial technology company with a US office, offering cloud-based electronic data capture and clinical trial management software, randomisation and supply tools to pharmaceutical firms and contract research organisations in China and abroad. Revenue comes from software subscriptions and services. B2B life-sciences software with no consumer awareness. The platform is used by pharma sponsors, hospitals and CROs to run trials efficiently, with customers mainly among Chinese drug developers, and the company also sells to global sponsors.

Chicago-based food biotechnology company behind Nature's Fynd, which ferments a fungal microbe discovered in Yellowstone National Park to produce Fy protein, sold as meatless breakfast patties, burgers and cream cheese alternatives in US supermarkets. It has raised hundreds of millions of dollars and was founded around 2012. Consumer food brand with growing but modest awareness among plant-based buyers. The product is made by fermentation in tanks, similar to brewing, and the range is sold in US grocery chains such as Whole Foods and Target.

Maryland biotechnology company (Nasdaq: VIE), formerly spun out of AstraZeneca and MedImmune, that developed Uplizna (inebilizumab) for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, an autoimmune neurological disease, sold to neurologists. Horizon Therapeutics acquired it in 2021 for roughly 3 billion dollars, and Amgen later bought Horizon in 2023. B2B, no consumer visibility. Uplizna was approved by the FDA in June 2020 and later extended to IgG4-related disease, selling at a high price per infusion, with customers mostly academic and community neurologists.

Guangzhou-based B2B online platform for pharmaceutical trading, connecting drug wholesalers and manufacturers with small pharmacies and clinics, providing ordering, logistics and credit services. It serves independent drugstores in China and earns margin and service fees. A fast-growing digital health marketplace with strong recognition among pharmacy owners, but little among the public. It started around 2014 and has built a large network of independent drugstores as customers, making it a recognised digital supplier in China's pharmaceutical distribution.

Texas medical device company (Nasdaq: APEN) focused on obesity treatments, notably the Orbera intragastric balloon and the Lap-Band adjustable gastric band, sold to bariatric surgeons and clinics in the US and abroad. Boston Scientific acquired it in 2023 for about 615 million dollars. B2B med-tech, though the Lap-Band name is known to patients. The business was a mid-sized medical devices firm with annual sales in the range of 70 million dollars, with Orbera and Lap-Band the biggest products.

Belgian molecular diagnostics company whose Idylla platform delivers rapid cancer genotyping and infectious disease tests from a small cartridge-based system, sold to hospitals and labs worldwide. It listed on Euronext Brussels in 2015 and ran into financial distress; the input flags the company as liquidated. B2B medical devices with no consumer awareness. Idylla tests are used to detect cancer mutations that decide on treatments for colorectal, lung and melanoma cancers, and the platform is used in labs in dozens of countries.

Biotechnology company with Chinese and US operations (Durham, North Carolina) developing treatments for infectious diseases including chronic hepatitis B and HIV, COVID-19 antibodies and other viral and CNS programmes. Listed in Hong Kong in 2021, it licenses and develops drugs across the US and China. Clinical-stage, so B2B with no consumer profile. It has significant operations in China (Beijing and Shanghai) and a US office in Durham, North Carolina.

Texas diagnostics company (Nasdaq: CSTL) known for DecisionDx-Melanoma, a gene expression profile test that estimates metastasis risk in skin cancer, plus tests for uveal melanoma, Barrett's oesophagus and dermatology conditions. Customers are physicians and pathologists, reimbursed by Medicare and private insurers, with revenue in the hundreds of millions of dollars. Founded 2007. B2B clinical lab, with little public awareness. The company's business revolves around skin cancer testing, which it can market directly to dermatologists and surgical oncologists, so it has built a focused sales force across the US.

Menlo Park drug delivery company (Nasdaq: CORI) that developed transdermal and transmucosal patches and sold contract manufacturing and licensed products such as the ADHD patch for Noven and others. Customers were large pharma partners. It was acquired in 2018 by Gurnet Point Capital and Juniper Pharmaceuticals for around 500 million dollars. B2B, no consumer brand. Its technology allowed delivery of drugs through the skin, which avoids pills, with patch manufacturing in Grand Rapids, Michigan.

Minnesota medical device company (Nasdaq: CVRX) selling the Barostim system, an implantable baroreflex activation therapy for patients with heart failure and resistant hypertension, to hospitals and cardiologists in the US and Europe. Revenue is tens of millions of dollars and growing. Founded in 2001. B2B medical technology, with little general consumer awareness. The system works like a pacemaker for blood pressure, with a pulse generator implanted below the collarbone and an electrode connected to the carotid sinus, and has FDA approval for heart failure since 2019.

Chinese biologics developer listed in Hong Kong that develops antibody drugs for cancer and autoimmune diseases, such as the PD-1 antibody geptanolimab and TNF-alpha antibody candidates. Customers are hospitals, with partnerships for rights in China and abroad. Revenue is small and losses persistent. B2B biotech with no consumer visibility. R&D and pilot manufacturing are based in China, and it listed in Hong Kong around 2020.

California population genomics and health company that sequences customers' exomes through health systems, employers and research programmes and operates a genomic data marketplace for partners such as pharma and research institutions. It built tests, apps and clinical programmes with large backing from investors and partners including Illumina. B2B and B2B2C platform with limited consumer brand awareness. Its flagship product is the Helix Exome+ test, and it has partnered with health systems such as Mount Sinai and Geisinger to roll out population sequencing programmes.

Bermuda-incorporated, Massachusetts-based biopharmaceutical company (Nasdaq: KNSA) selling Arcalyst (rilonacept) for recurrent pericarditis, a rare heart inflammation, generating revenue of several hundred million dollars from specialist cardiologists and rheumatologists in the US. It also develops follow-on antibody therapies and obtained rights from Regeneron. B2B healthcare with no consumer awareness. Kiniksa was started by the Baker Bros investment group in 2015, and the company has little general brand visibility.

Cambridge, Massachusetts biotech developing antibody-drug conjugates and conditioning therapies to prepare patients for stem cell transplants, with candidates such as MGTA-117. It listed on Nasdaq (MGTA) in 2018 and merged with Dianthus Therapeutics in 2023 after cutting its programmes. Clinical-stage biotech, no consumer awareness. The company was founded in 2015, and raised funds from investors, while its shares fell sharply after trial data, leading to the merger with a private biotech and a reverse listing.

New Jersey in vitro diagnostics company providing blood typing, immunoassay and clinical chemistry systems and reagents to hospitals, labs and blood banks in 125 countries. It was carved out of Johnson & Johnson by Carlyle in 2014, listed on Nasdaq (OCDX) in 2021 and merged with Quidel in 2022 to form QuidelOrtho. Revenue was about 2 billion dollars. B2B, no consumer visibility.

Boston company that pioneered prescription digital therapeutics, FDA-authorised software treatments such as reSET for substance use disorder (the first of its kind in 2017), reSET-O for opioid use disorder and Somryst for chronic insomnia. It sold to clinicians and payers and listed on Nasdaq (PEAR) through a 2021 SPAC merger. Slow insurer reimbursement led to a Chapter 11 filing in April 2023, and its assets were sold, including to Nox Health. Defunct as an independent business.

Newark, California clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company (Nasdaq: PTGX) built on peptide drug discovery. Its lead programmes are rusfertide, an injectable hepcidin mimetic for polycythemia vera developed with Takeda, and icotrokinra (JNJ-2113), an oral IL-23 receptor antagonist peptide partnered with Johnson & Johnson for psoriasis and ulcerative colitis. Revenue is collaboration and milestone based, so it has no marketed product of its own to patients yet. B2B biotech with no consumer brand.

Jiangsu-based vaccine developer, listed in Hong Kong, working on recombinant vaccines including a 9-valent HPV candidate, a recombinant shingles vaccine and adjuvant technology. It is still pre-revenue and relies on clinical trial progress in China. Customers will ultimately be Chinese provincial disease-control centres and private vaccination clinics. B2B life-science company with no consumer brand recognition yet. Its candidates compete with Merck's Gardasil and with HPV vaccines from domestic Chinese rivals.

Canadian forest products company with newsprint, market pulp, tissue, wood products and specialty papers, selling to publishers, building product distributors and converters in North America and globally, operating mills in Quebec, Ontario and the US. It had revenues of roughly 3 to 4 billion dollars and listed on the NYSE and TSX (RFP). Paper Excellence, the Indonesian-linked group that already owned Domtar, acquired it in March 2023 for around 2.7 billion dollars. B2B, no consumer brand.

Cambridge, Massachusetts biotech founded by Flagship Pioneering that tried to engineer red blood cells as a platform for cell therapies against cancer, autoimmune and rare disease. It listed on Nasdaq (RUBY) in 2018 and raised heavily from investors, but cut back after poor clinical progress and wound down operations in 2023. No marketed products and no consumer presence. Its approach, called Red Cell Therapeutics, used genetically engineered red cell precursors as carriers.

Lexington, Massachusetts messenger RNA therapeutics company that was developing treatments for cystic fibrosis (MRT5005) and for primary ciliary dyskinesia, and mRNA vaccine programmes in partnership with Sanofi. It listed on Nasdaq (TBIO) and was acquired by Sanofi in September 2021 for roughly 3.2 billion dollars to build Sanofi's mRNA centre of excellence. B2B biotech with no consumer profile. It also built mRNA manufacturing capacity in Massachusetts.

California medical technology company (Nasdaq: AFIB) selling the AcQMap high-resolution 3D cardiac imaging and mapping system for treating complex arrhythmias such as atrial fibrillation, as well as catheters and left-heart access tools. Customers are hospitals and electrophysiologists. The company shrank its business in 2023 and sold its left-heart access line to Medtronic. B2B med-tech with no consumer profile. Acutus was founded in 2011 and listed on Nasdaq in 2020.

Biotechnology company in Beijing, with a US operation near Boston, known for its RenMice fully human antibody discovery platform and its large library of knockout and humanised mouse models for drug development. It earns revenue from licensing antibodies, selling models and services to pharmaceutical and biotech customers, and listed in Hong Kong around 2022. B2B research services with no consumer awareness.

South San Francisco oncology biotech (Nasdaq: CALA) that developed drugs targeting tumour metabolism and immune suppression, including telaglenastat, a glutaminase inhibitor, and sapanisertib. Late-stage trials did not succeed and the company wound down in 2023 and liquidated. Work was previously supported by partnerships with Incyte. No sales and no consumer exposure. Calithera was founded in 2010 and listed on Nasdaq in 2014, partnering earlier with Incyte on an arginase inhibitor.

Austrian commercial real estate group, headquartered in Vienna, owning and developing office buildings and some logistics and hotel properties in Austria, Germany and Central and Eastern Europe, especially Berlin, Munich, Frankfurt, Prague, Warsaw and Budapest. Listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange, with CPI Property Group the largest shareholder after Starwood sold its stake. Rental income from corporate tenants is the main revenue, with a portfolio of several billion euros. B2B landlord with low consumer visibility.

Pennsylvania-based contract development and manufacturing organisation for cell and gene therapies, offering plasmid DNA, viral vector production and process development services to biotech customers from sites in the Philadelphia area. SK Group's SK pharmteco bought it in 2022 and combined it into a global CDMO platform alongside other holdings. B2B manufacturing partner, no consumer brand. It operates under the SK pharmteco umbrella with sites in the US, Europe and Asia.

Yonkers, New York clinical-stage biotech (Nasdaq: CFRX) developing biologic treatments against drug-resistant infections, led by exebacase, a lysin enzyme targeting Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infections, and antibody-based candidates. Late-stage results failed to win approval and the company filed for Chapter 11 in December 2023. B2B only, no consumer presence. ContraFect was founded in 2008 and relied on investors and public markets rather than product sales, so its revenue was negligible. Its pipeline aimed at infections that antibiotics cannot treat.

Columbus, Ohio gene therapy contract development and manufacturing organisation specialising in adeno-associated virus vectors, working with biotech developers on clinical and commercial supply from its Ohio manufacturing campus. Japan's Ajinomoto acquired it in 2023 for about 620 million dollars to expand its biopharma CDMO business. B2B only, low public brand awareness. It was founded in 2010 and has been linked to Nationwide Children's Hospital in Columbus.

Boston AI pathology company whose platform, AISight and related tools, helps pathologists interpret slides and supports pharma clinical trials by scoring biomarkers, with large partnerships including Bristol Myers Squibb and Roche. It also owns a clinical diagnostics laboratory, and is venture backed by investors including General Catalyst, Tiger Global and Softbank. B2B healthcare AI with no general consumer awareness. It remains privately held.

Pure Harvest Smart Farms is a tech-enabled agribusiness based in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, working in agriculture and agtech farming according to the input. The input does not say which crops it grows, how large it is, or who owns it. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Thousand Oaks Biopharmaceuticals is a biopharmaceutical company based in Haimen, Jiangsu, China, according to the input. The record gives no product names, trial stage, ownership or scale. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Redwood City clinical-stage biotech (Nasdaq: ALLK) developing antibodies against Siglec-8, a receptor on mast cells and eosinophils, in allergic and inflammatory diseases. Its lead lirentelimab was tested in eosinophilic gastritis and other conditions but failed a pivotal trial in 2023, after which the company cut staff sharply. Pre-revenue and B2B, with no consumer profile. Allakos was founded in 2012 and listed on Nasdaq in 2018, and later cut staff.

Florida fertiliser manufacturer making enhanced efficiency, organic-based granular fertilisers from biosolids such as the Class A product SC27 and the Biosolids-based Nutrisoil, sold to farms, golf courses, turf managers and growers. It recycles municipal waste into plant nutrients and supplies agricultural distributors and turf customers in the US. B2B agricultural input supplier with limited public visibility. Its base in Central Florida suits biosolids recycling and citrus-area fertiliser sales.

Somerville, Massachusetts drug discovery company founded by Flagship Pioneering that uses single-cell and AI-driven analysis of how cells behave to design therapies, with an emerging programme for sickle cell disease and other early-stage programmes. It is privately held with venture backing and has a partnership with Novo Nordisk. B2B biotech with no consumer awareness. Cellarity was formed in 2019 and has raised large venture rounds from investors including Flagship.

Cambridge, Massachusetts oncology data and software company providing real-world data, AI analytics and clinical trial tools to biopharma, with partnerships with firms such as Pfizer and AstraZeneca, and oncology records from hospital networks. Backed by Thoma Bravo and Anaxa. Revenue comes from SaaS subscriptions and data licences. B2B healthtech with little consumer profile. It was started in 2017 and has expanded through acquisitions of data and technology businesses.

Chicago clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing ecopipam, a first-in-class dopamine D1 antagonist, for Tourette syndrome and other neuropsychiatric conditions in children. It is backed by the Chicago-based biotech company builder Paragon Biosciences and has shown positive late-stage data. Pre-revenue and private, serving neurologists through future clinical channels. No consumer presence. Emalex was started in 2018 and the Tourette market currently relies on older antipsychotic drugs with side effects, so an alternative would be significant.

Enavate Sciences is a New York-based health care and life sciences company that, according to the input, invests in and supports health ventures. The record does not describe specific holdings, funds or scale. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

UK gene therapy developer in Stevenage, using AAV vectors for inherited diseases, with candidates for Gaucher disease and Fabry disease and earlier work in haemophilia. It listed on Nasdaq (FRLN) in 2021 and was taken private by Syncona in 2023 after losing funding. Clinical-stage biotech with no consumer profile. Freeline was founded in 2015 as a spin-off from University College London research and was backed by Syncona before the 2023 buyout.

Boston and Israel-based cell therapy company (Nasdaq: GMDA) that developed Omisirge (omidubicel), an umbilical cord blood-derived product approved by the FDA in April 2023 for blood cancer patients needing a transplant, and NK cell programmes. It sold to transplant centres and faced financial pressure and a delisting and restructuring in 2024. B2B oncology, no consumer exposure. Gamida's technology expands umbilical cord blood stem cells.

Boston company with production in Italy that marketed Plenity, an FDA-cleared oral hydrogel capsule for weight management, available by prescription and sold directly to consumers online and through telehealth. It listed on the NYSE (GLS) through a 2022 SPAC merger and filed for Chapter 11 in October 2023. It ran direct-to-consumer advertising. Business is now defunct, though the Plenity name was acquired by another firm.

Large Indian pharmaceutical company, private and family-owned, that makes generics, biosimilars and contract pharma at plants in India and Europe, selling through its European arm Accord Healthcare and in the US via Accord, with sales of several billion dollars. It manufactures for global brands and supplies hospitals and pharmacies. B2B generic manufacturer with moderate consumer recognition in India and Europe.

Specialty generic pharmaceutical business headquartered in Dubai that develops and commercialises hospital-focused and specialty generic injectables and oncology medicines for markets in the Middle East, Africa and Asia. It sells to hospitals, wholesalers and government tenders. Privately held and relatively small. B2B with no consumer brand. Its portfolio is aimed at the Gulf and wider emerging markets where hospital tenders favour affordable products. It is relatively small, privately owned and has no consumer brand.

Canadian operator of community pharmacies, building a network of independent and banner pharmacies across Ontario and other provinces that dispense prescription medicines, give vaccinations, run clinical services and sell over-the-counter and wellness items. It is headquartered in Toronto and grew by buying independent pharmacies. Local brand recognition in neighbourhoods rather than a national retail name. Pharmacy chains in Canada are regulated provincially, so such networks tend to operate under local banners.

Watertown, Massachusetts RNA therapeutics company developing engineered circular RNA medicines and lipid nanoparticle delivery, for in vivo cell engineering and immune cell reprogramming. It launched in 2022 with venture funding from ARCH Venture and others. Pre-clinical stage, with no marketed products and no consumer profile. Circular RNA is more stable than linear mRNA, so the platform aims at longer-lasting protein expression and lower doses, and the company also develops its own delivery technology. Customers would be pharma partners and, eventually, patients through physicians.

AI company for biomedicine, headquartered in New York and Paris, using federated learning to train models on hospital data without moving patient records. It runs partnerships with Sanofi, Servier and AstraZeneca, and developed tools such as K Navigator, an AI assistant for researchers. Revenue comes from pharma collaborations and software. B2B only, little general awareness outside healthcare and AI circles.

Indianapolis clinical-stage radiopharmaceutical company (Nasdaq: PNT) developing targeted radioligand therapies including PNT2002 (lutetium-177 PSMA) for prostate cancer. Eli Lilly acquired it in late 2023 for about 1.4 billion dollars. Its work was supported by manufacturing in the US and Canada. B2B biotech with no consumer profile. It listed on Nasdaq in 2021, and the sale gave Lilly a late-stage radioligand asset for oncology, where Novartis's Pluvicto is the main marketed rival.

Cambridge, Massachusetts therapeutics platform company founded by Flagship Pioneering, focused on nanoparticle-based delivery systems that use naturally derived materials to carry drugs to specific tissues, such as the gut and immune cells. Privately held and early stage, with partnership potential for pharma. B2B only, no consumer presence. Its work targets the gut and the immune system, and as a Flagship company it is funded by venture capital rather than revenue.

Clinical-stage biotech with US and China roots, developing treatments for neurodegenerative and eye diseases such as glaucoma and age-related neurodegeneration, based on programmes targeting cell survival mechanisms. It is venture funded and early stage, selling nothing to patients yet. B2B only, with no consumer profile. Sironax is private and pre-revenue, and its backers are venture funds. Customers would eventually be neurologists and ophthalmologists, with licensing deals as an earlier route to revenue. Its profile is low outside the biotech investor community.

Irish farmer-owned dairy and agribusiness co-operative based in Kilkenny, renamed Tirlan in 2022 from Glanbia Co-operative Society after selling down its stake in Glanbia plc. It collects milk from thousands of member farms, makes dairy ingredients, and sells consumer brands such as Avonmore milk plus animal feed, fertiliser and grain to farmers. Revenue is above 2 billion euros. Known to Irish farmers and consumers, with a record of regional sponsorship, but not widely outside Ireland.

Seattle-based non-profit research institute founded in 2003 by Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen, focused on mapping the brain, including the Allen Brain Atlas, and publishing open data on neuroscience, cells and circuits for researchers worldwide. It is funded by philanthropy and grants rather than selling products. Known in the neuroscience community, with limited consumer profile. The institute also runs related units such as the Allen Institute for Cell Science under the same umbrella.

Evanston, Illinois clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company (Nasdaq: APTX) developing small-molecule modulators of the NMDA receptor for pain and neuropsychiatric disorders, spun out of Northwestern University research. Its candidates failed key trials and it wound down and dissolved around 2023. No marketed products and no consumer profile. Aptinyx was founded in 2015 and listed on Nasdaq in 2018. Its candidates, including NYX-2925 for pain, did not show enough benefit in trials to justify further spending, leaving it without a viable pipeline.

Austin biotech (Nasdaq: SAVA) developing simufilam for Alzheimer's disease, a drug that failed its Phase 3 trials in 2024 after years of scrutiny over data integrity and an SEC settlement. It has no marketed products and a retail-investor shareholder base. B2B biotech with a high public profile in investing circles but no consumer brand. Cassava Sciences was formerly named Pain Therapeutics until 2019.

Vancouver- and Seattle-based kidney disease biotech (Nasdaq: KDNY) developing atrasentan and other drugs for IgA nephropathy and other rare chronic kidney diseases. Novartis acquired Chinook in 2023 for about 3.5 billion dollars. Customers would be nephrologists. B2B and pre-commercial, so no consumer profile. Chinook came together through a merger with Aduro Biotech in 2020, and Novartis gained atrasentan and zigakibart through the deal.

Cambridge, Massachusetts biotech (Nasdaq: CDAK) developing engineered exosomes as a drug delivery platform for cancer and inflammatory diseases, with partnerships including with Jazz Pharmaceuticals. It failed to raise enough capital to continue and filed for bankruptcy in 2023. No marketed products, no consumer exposure. Codiak was founded in 2015, and exoSTING and exoIL-12 were its lead programmes. Failure to raise money led to Chapter 11.

Lexington, Massachusetts drug developer (Nasdaq: CNCE) using deuterium chemistry to modify existing drugs. Its lead was deuruxolitinib (CTP-543) for alopecia areata. Sun Pharma acquired it in 2023 for about 576 million dollars and launched the drug as Leqselvi. Customers are dermatologists; B2B pharma with little consumer awareness. Concert was founded in 2006 and, before deuruxolitinib, had licensed the deuterated drug Austedo to Teva, which earned royalties.

Vancouver-based clinical-stage oncology company (Nasdaq: EPIX) developing masofaniten, an oral androgen receptor N-terminal domain inhibitor for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Development was stopped in 2024 after limited trial results, and the company has since explored strategic options. B2B biotech with no consumer profile. The drug aimed to overcome resistance to treatments such as enzalutamide in men with advanced prostate cancer. ESSA had no marketed products, and funds were held mostly in cash after development was halted.

Georgia-based supplier of self-storage building products, including roll-up doors, hallway systems, relocatable storage units and smart access technology, selling to storage developers, owners and contractors in North America, Europe, Australia and the Middle East. Listed on the NYSE (JBI) via a 2021 SPAC merger, with revenue near 1 billion dollars. Customers include Public Storage and Extra Space. B2B with no consumer awareness.

Indonesian cable broadband and pay-TV operator in the Lippo group, running the First Media and Link Net brands, with fibre and cable networks in Jakarta and other Indonesian cities. It supplies home internet, pay-TV and enterprise connectivity and was listed on the Indonesian stock exchange, with subscribers in the hundreds of thousands to over a million. Known to Indonesian households as an ISP.

UK retirement housebuilder that builds and sells apartments for older people under the McCarthy & Stone and Retirement Care brands, in schemes with communal lounges and managed services. It is based in Bournemouth, has sold thousands of homes and was listed on the London Stock Exchange for some time before changing ownership. Customers are people over 60. Brand is well known to older UK consumers.

Argentine agribusiness processing soybeans and other oilseeds, crushing them into meal and oil for export through its port-linked plants in Santa Fe and other provinces, selling to international trading companies and food manufacturers. It is controlled by the Perez Companc family and is the agricultural arm of Molinos Rio de la Plata. B2B commodity processor with little consumer branding. Argentina's farm export sector is a major source of national foreign currency.

Chicago-based biotech holding and company-builder, founded by entrepreneur Jeffrey Aronin, that creates and funds specialised drug development companies such as Emalex and others. It combines capital, management and shared services to take products from research to market. Privately held. B2B healthcare investor, little public profile. Paragon's portfolio companies have included gene-silencing, neuropsychiatry and rare disease developers, and it runs its own labs in Chicago. Aronin earlier built Ovation Pharmaceuticals, later sold to Lundbeck in 2009.

Cambridge, Massachusetts oncology biotech developing small-molecule inhibitors of PARP7 (RBN-2397) and other cancer therapies, based on research on ADP-ribosylation. Privately held and venture funded, with early clinical studies in solid tumours. B2B and pre-revenue, with no consumer exposure. PARP7 inhibition aims to restore the interferon signalling that tumours suppress, which is also a route to making cancers more visible to the immune system. The company is private, venture backed and years from market, so it has no consumer brand and no commercial products.

California and China-linked diagnostics company developing cell-free DNA tests for early cancer detection and screening using methylation signatures, working with hospitals and labs in China and elsewhere. Privately held with venture backing, selling to clinicians and screening programmes rather than directly to consumers. Low public profile. Singlera also operates in China, where early detection screening for cancers such as colorectal and liver is a major focus. Its methylation tests are sold to laboratories and healthcare institutions.

Belgian biomanufacturing group founded in 2014 that developed compact, low-cost continuous bioprocess systems, notably the NevoLine system for producing vaccines and biologics, aimed at making vaccines more affordable in emerging markets. Customers are biopharma and public health bodies. Its technology unit was sold to Merck KGaA in 2021. B2B with little consumer profile. Univercells was started in Belgium and works with international health organisations.

Fremont, California specialty pharma (Nasdaq: ZSAN) that developed a microneedle patch system for delivery of drugs through the skin, with Qtrypta (zolmitriptan) for acute migraine as the lead. After FDA delays and funding problems it filed for Chapter 11 in 2022. B2B and defunct, with no consumer exposure. Zosano was founded in 2006 and listed on Nasdaq in 2015. Its microneedle array applies drug through the skin from a single-use patch, where Qtrypta had been delayed by manufacturing observations.

San Francisco biotech developing AIO-001, a long-acting anti-TSLP antibody for asthma and other respiratory diseases, licensed from Jiangsu Hengrui and moving through clinical trials. GSK acquired it in 2023 for around 1 billion dollars up front, giving GSK an alternative to its existing respiratory drugs, with additional milestone payments possible. TSLP is a key upstream driver of airway inflammation. B2B drug developer, with no consumer profile.

German genetic diagnostics company in Rostock offering testing for rare and genetic diseases and a large biodata platform used by pharma partners for drug discovery. Listed on Nasdaq (CNTG) and operating across the Middle East, Europe and Asia, with customers including physicians, hospitals and drug developers. It has been loss-making for most of its history. B2B diagnostics, with no consumer brand and low public profile.

Cambridge, Massachusetts neuroscience biotech (Nasdaq: CYCN), spun out of Ironwood in 2019, developing soluble guanylate cyclase stimulators for central nervous system diseases. It cut programmes after trial setbacks and ultimately merged and reorganised. Clinical-stage and B2B, with no consumer awareness. Cyclerion started in 2019 as a separation from Ironwood's research arm, with a pipeline of treatments for CNS disorders and the compound zagociguat for mitochondrial disease. It later reorganised and its shares fell sharply, so it is a very small company without product sales.

La Jolla cancer diagnostics company known for its circulating tumour cell platform that analyses cells from a blood sample, including the AR-V7 test in prostate cancer co-developed with Genomic Health. It sold to oncologists, pharma trial sponsors and labs. Privately held with venture backing. B2B diagnostics with no consumer awareness. Its technology images millions of blood cells to find and characterise rare tumour cells, helping doctors decide whether certain prostate cancer drugs will work. Revenue comes from lab testing and pharma partnerships.

Canadian radiopharmaceutical company in Hamilton, Ontario (Nasdaq: FUSN) developing alpha-emitting actinium-225 targeted therapies for cancer, with lead FPI-2265 for prostate cancer. AstraZeneca acquired it in 2024 for about 2.4 billion dollars. Clinical-stage, so B2B with no consumer profile. Fusion was founded in 2017 and partnered with AstraZeneca before the sale. Actinium-225 emits alpha particles that damage tumour cells with a short range. It had no marketed products. After the deal it became part of AstraZeneca's growing oncology radioconjugate portfolio.

Boston vaccine biotech (Nasdaq: HLVX) that developed HIL-214, a norovirus vaccine candidate from Takeda's programme, for infants. The main late-stage trial failed in 2024, after which the company cut staff and sought alternatives. B2B and clinical-stage, with no marketed products and no consumer exposure. HilleVax was formed in 2020 around a Takeda-licensed vaccine and listed on Nasdaq in 2022. Norovirus causes widespread gastroenteritis and no vaccine exists, so success would have been a large opportunity. After the trial miss, the company explored alternatives.

Seattle vaccine biotech developing virus-like particle vaccines against RSV and human metapneumovirus, built on University of Washington technology. AstraZeneca acquired it in late 2023 for up to roughly 1.1 billion dollars after it listed on Nasdaq (ICVX). B2B and clinical-stage, with no consumer presence. Icosavax licensed its protein engineering from the Institute for Protein Design in Seattle, and its VLP technology aimed to produce stronger responses from adults over 60. The deal put AstraZeneca in competition with GSK's and Pfizer's RSV vaccines.

Canadian-US health technology company (Nasdaq: MDVL) that built self-service pharmacy kiosks, MedCenter, placed in clinics and medical offices, letting patients collect prescriptions on site, and later moved to digital prescription fulfilment. It was loss-making and wound down in the early 2020s. Little consumer brand awareness. MedAvail's kiosks were deployed in medical clinics with pharmacist oversight by video. It later also provided a technology platform to pharmacies. Funding problems ended the business.

Baltimore mobile advertising platform (NYSE: MM) that helped app publishers and advertisers buy and sell mobile ad space through real-time bidding, with a self-serve tool and mobile data. AOL (Verizon) acquired it in 2015 for about 238 million dollars. B2B ad tech, with little consumer visibility, and absorbed into Verizon's media business. Millennial Media was founded in 2006 and listed on the NYSE in 2012. It was one of the earliest ad networks specialising in mobile.

North Carolina dermatology-focused biotech (Nasdaq: NOVN) developing nitric oxide-based treatments, notably berdazimer gel for molluscum contagiosum, approved by the FDA in 2024 as Zelsuvmi. It filed for Chapter 11 in 2023 and later sold the business to Ligand Pharmaceuticals in 2024. B2B pharma with no consumer profile. Zelsuvmi is a topical treatment for a contagious skin infection that affects children and adults. Novan also had earlier antiviral and acne programmes, and a topical nitric oxide technology.

One-stop contract research and manufacturing service for cell and gene therapy and biologics, with sites in New Jersey, China and the UK, offering plasmid, viral vector, mRNA and cell line services to drug developers. It is a subsidiary of Chinese life-sciences group GenScript, operating under the GenScript ProBio brand. B2B outsourcing partner, no consumer profile. It supports clients through lab sites in the US and Asia.

San Diego biotech (Nasdaq: RPHM) developing mavodelpar, a PPAR delta agonist for primary mitochondrial myopathies. The main trial failed in 2023 and the company merged in 2024 with OnKure Therapeutics. Pre-revenue and B2B, with no consumer exposure. Reneo listed on Nasdaq in 2021. Mitochondrial myopathies are rare genetic diseases that cause muscle weakness, and there is no approved therapy. The company's reverse merger with OnKure brought a new focus on precision oncology.

California thin-film solar company that made copper indium gallium diselenide (CIGS) solar modules and supplied them to utilities and commercial projects, with a factory in Mississippi. It raised significant venture funding but struggled against falling Chinese module prices and ceased operations in the mid-2010s. B2B and defunct, no consumer profile. Its pitch was efficiency and low-light performance, but module prices fell sharply as Chinese rivals expanded.

Super-Max is a manufacturing company based in Dubai that specialises in personal care products, according to the input. The record does not say which products or markets, nor how large it is. Not to be confused with similarly named Indian or Malaysian firms. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Dublin-based clinical-stage biotech developing emactuzumab, an antibody that targets CSF1R, for tenosynovial giant cell tumour, a rare joint tumour, and other inflammatory joint diseases. It is venture funded and early commercial planning has been described. B2B pharma with no consumer profile. TGCT is a rare tumour of the joint lining that often needs surgery. SynOx's drug works by blocking the CSF1R receptor and was in-licensed from Roche. The company is venture funded and has no sales.

Municipal authority supplying drinking water, sewer collection and stormwater management to Pittsburgh and some surrounding communities, serving several hundred thousand people. It was created as a public authority in 1984 and is overseen by the city, with a board appointed locally, and finances itself through rates and bonds. Public-sector utility with a well-known local brand but no commercial sponsorship role.

Foster City early-stage biotherapeutics company developing antibodies against galectin-3 and other targets for neurodegenerative disease and cancer, including a candidate for Alzheimer's. Privately held with venture funding and no marketed products. B2B only, no consumer profile. Galectin-3 is a protein linked to inflammation and tissue damage, and TrueBinding wants to block it with antibodies. The company is early-stage and based in the Bay Area, with funding from life-science investors. It is far from approval and has no consumer-facing product.

Shanghai-based contract research firm that provides structure-based drug discovery services, protein crystallography and chemistry to pharmaceutical and biotech clients worldwide, plus equity investments in its customers' pipelines. Listed in Hong Kong (1873). Revenue comes from fee-for-service work and licensing. B2B only, little public awareness. Viva Biotech works on early discovery for many clients and also does licensing. It was founded in 2008. Customers are drug developers rather than consumers.

Spanish pharmaceutical company based in Barcelona, specialising in medical dermatology, with products such as Ilumetri (tildrakizumab) for psoriasis and the licensed lebrikizumab (Ebglyss) for atopic dermatitis in Europe, sold to dermatologists across Europe and the US. It is listed on the Spanish stock exchange and was founded in 1943, with revenue over 900 million euros. Prescription-focused, so mainly B2B though the name is known to Spanish consumers.

Cleveland regenerative medicine company (Nasdaq: ATHX) that developed MultiStem, an adult stem cell therapy, for ischaemic stroke and acute respiratory distress, with Healios of Japan as its partner. Late-stage stroke results fell short and the company filed for Chapter 11 in January 2024. B2B and defunct, no consumer awareness. MultiStem cells are taken from adult bone marrow and were meant to reduce inflammation after injury. Athersys was founded in 1995 and had cut staff before bankruptcy.

Rhode Island not-for-profit health system built around Women & Infants Hospital, Kent Hospital and Butler Hospital, a psychiatric hospital, plus affiliated physician groups and the Care New England Medical Group. It serves patients across Rhode Island and southeastern Massachusetts, and revenue comes from hospital care billed to insurers and Medicare and Medicaid. Women & Infants, one of the biggest US maternity hospitals, is its flagship, and it has teaching ties to Brown University. Strong local brand, but sponsorship activity is community and philanthropic.

Texas telecommunications equipment maker that designed optical core routers for carrier networks, aiming to sell high-capacity routers to telecom operators and internet backbone providers around the dot-com era. It raised large venture funding and had a multi-hundred-million-dollar valuation at its peak, but the telecoms collapse of 2001-2003 undermined demand, and it was sold off in the mid-2000s. B2B with no consumer profile, now defunct.

Washington State company selling hydroponic equipment, grow lights, nutrients and cultivation supplies to indoor growers through its retail and online brands, with a focus on cannabis cultivation. Customers are commercial and small-scale growers and hobbyists across the US and Canada. It trades on the OTC market (PHOT) and was later involved in mushroom and other cultivation businesses. Small company with niche brand awareness among growers and no mainstream consumer profile.

Boston clinical-stage oncology company (Nasdaq: IKNA) that used a platform called Kynnecta to find drug targets in tumours, with candidates such as IK-175, an AHR inhibitor, and IK-930, a TEAD inhibitor. It was funded by venture investors and an IPO in 2021, and merged with Inmagene Biopharmaceuticals in 2023 and then pivoted to a different pipeline. B2B biotech, no consumer presence.

India's second-largest IT services company, a Bengaluru-based consulting, digital transformation, cloud and outsourcing group with about 320,000 employees and annual revenue of roughly 19 billion dollars. Clients are large banks, insurers, manufacturers, retailers and governments across North America and Europe. It also sells Finacle banking software and Topaz AI services. Founded in 1981 and listed on the NSE, BSE and NYSE (INFY). Strong B2B brand and a known sponsor of tennis and cricket.

Finnish forest industry group owned by about 90,000 Finnish forest owners through the Metsäliitto co-operative, with revenue of roughly 5 to 6 billion euros. Businesses include Metsä Board (folding boxboard and packaging), Metsä Fibre (pulp and sawn timber), Metsä Tissue (Lambi and Serla tissue brands) and Metsä Wood (engineered timber). Customers are packaging converters, brand owners and consumers in Europe. Consumer brands are visible in Nordic supermarkets, though the group is mostly B2B.

American generic pharmaceutical developer and maker, with a base in the New York area, supplying oral solid doses and other generic products to wholesalers and pharmacies, mostly in the US. Customers buy under the company name and private labels. A small, low-profile generics maker with no consumer brand and limited public data. Generic drugs typically compete on price and approvals, and such firms sell to the big US drug wholesalers and retail chains. No public figures are available for revenue or headcount, which suggests a small operation.

Texas clinical-stage biotech developing RBT-1 for the prevention of complications after cardiac surgery such as acute kidney injury, and a programme for kidney disease. It is privately held and venture funded. Customers will eventually be cardiac surgeons and hospitals, and revenue is zero so far. B2B and pre-commercial, with no consumer profile. The kidney injury market after surgery has no approved drug today, which is the commercial opportunity it chases.

Tianjin-based Chinese state-owned maker of seamless steel pipes, one of the world's largest, serving the oil and gas industry with casing, tubing and line pipe, as well as boiler and automotive pipes. It sells to oil majors and service companies in China and abroad, with an annual capacity of several million tonnes. Under local government ownership with listed arms. B2B industrial company with no consumer profile.

Watertown, Massachusetts gene editing company that developed programmable genomic integration to insert large DNA sequences at chosen locations, aiming at cell therapies and genetic diseases. It launched in 2021 with large venture funding, and shut down in 2024 after failing to raise further money. Pre-clinical and B2B, with no consumer profile. Tome was started by veterans of the CRISPR field, and its technology aimed to avoid the cutting of DNA that standard gene editing uses.

La Jolla algae biotechnology company, formerly Synthetic Genomics, that engineered microalgae to produce biofuels and other products, with a long partnership with ExxonMobil. It also sold bioscience products and research in the past and has used genomics to optimise productivity. Privately held, research-focused and B2B, with no consumer profile. Algae can grow on non-arable land using sunlight and carbon dioxide, which is why oil companies funded the research. Today the firm focuses on algae strains and tools for sustainable products, with limited revenue.

Singapore-based agribusiness group, among Asia's largest, processing and trading palm oil, edible oils, sugar, rice, flour and oilseeds, with plantations in Indonesia and Malaysia and refineries across China, India and Africa. It sells to consumers under Fortune cooking oil in China and brands such as Arawana, and to food manufacturers. Revenue is about 65 billion dollars. Listed on the SGX (F34) and founded in 1991 by Kuok Khoon Hong and Martua Sitorus. Strong consumer brands in Asia.

Cambridge, Massachusetts biotech that studies transposable elements, the repetitive 'jumping' genes in the human genome, and their role in disease, developing drugs for autoimmune and inflammatory conditions and cancer. It is privately held with venture funding and no marketed products. B2B only, with no consumer profile. Transposable elements make up roughly half of human DNA, and the company argues they drive inflammation and cancer. It is a young firm with a small team and no products on sale.

Cambridge, Massachusetts biotech founded by Flagship Pioneering that develops protein nanoparticles to deliver gene editing and genetic medicines safely to targeted cells in the body. Privately held, venture-funded and pre-clinical, with partnership opportunities for pharma. B2B only and no consumer profile. Aera is a young company from Flagship, which also launched Moderna, and the approach is designed to avoid the delivery limits of viral vectors and lipid particles. It is early in development and has no products for sale.

AeroSafe Global is a Rochester, New York company in biopharma and manufacturing that, according to the input, develops aerogels for use in various applications. The record does not say which products, customers or scale. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Atom Bioscience & Pharmaceutical is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in Suzhou, Jiangsu, China, according to the input. No products, partners or ownership are described. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Bulgarian cement producer in Devnya, near Varna on the Black Sea, with a large cement plant plus the Devnya Cement and related concrete operations, supplying construction firms and building materials distributors across Bulgaria and neighbouring Balkan markets. It belongs to the Italcementi group, which HeidelbergCement (now Heidelberg Materials) acquired in 2016. B2B industrial company with no consumer brand. It is among the largest cement producers in Bulgaria, serving customers in housing, roads and infrastructure.

Boston clinical-stage oncology company (Nasdaq: ELEV) that developed targeted cancer drugs, first seribantumab for tumours with NRG1 gene fusions, then EO-3021, an antibody-drug conjugate for gastric cancer targeting Claudin 18.2. It was loss-making with no revenue, and the programmes were later wound down or sold. B2B biotech with no consumer presence. Elevation Oncology was based in New York before moving to Boston, listed on Nasdaq in 2021 and relied entirely on equity funding rather than sales.

Austin health research company that runs a network of community physician practices as clinical trial sites and combines it with real-world data and technology, connecting pharmaceutical sponsors with patients in everyday care. Revenue comes from sponsor contracts and data services. Private and venture backed. B2B only, with no consumer brand. Its model puts research into familiar local doctors' offices, which is meant to enrol more diverse and rural patients than big academic centres can.

Indianapolis cloud marketing software company that sold email marketing, social and mobile campaign tools, including Interactive Marketing Hub, to brands and agencies. It listed on the NYSE (ET) in 2012 and was acquired by Salesforce in 2013 for about 2.5 billion dollars, becoming the basis of Salesforce Marketing Cloud. B2B software, known to marketers but not to consumers, and now folded into Salesforce.

Ignis Therapeutics is a Chinese biotechnology company based in Shanghai, described in the input as developing innovative therapies. No product, pipeline or investor detail is available. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Innovance is a manufacturing company in Albert Lea, Minnesota that describes itself as 100 percent employee-owned through an ESOP, according to the input. The record does not say what it makes or who its customers are. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Phoenix nutrition and biotechnology company that makes bovine colostrum-based and immune-support ingredients, selling products such as DiaResQ for digestive health and supplying them to nutrition brands and healthcare providers. Revenue comes from ingredient sales and branded medical foods. Small privately held company. Sold mostly B2B, though DiaResQ reaches consumers. PanTheryx was founded in the 2010s and uses fermentation and processing from dairy sources to make products for digestive disorders. It works with health professionals and nutrition companies in the US and abroad.

Chengdu-based Chinese developer of nanopore gene sequencing technology and instruments, working to provide a domestic alternative to long-read sequencers from Oxford Nanopore for research labs, hospitals and genetic testing companies. Privately held and venture backed, with products in an early commercial stage. B2B life science tools, with little public recognition. The company is one of the new domestic sequencing instrument makers set up as China builds its own genomic technology supply chain, with a focus on real-time, portable devices and direct detection of DNA and RNA. Funding has come from technology investors.

St. John's United is a senior care provider in Billings, Montana, according to the input, offering assisted living, outpatient physical therapy and charity services. The input gives no capacity or ownership details. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Customer care and business process outsourcing company running multilingual call centres for technology, telecom and consumer clients around the world, with tens of thousands of agents. It was Boston-based and later merged with Stream's Eagan, Minnesota operations before Convergys acquired it in 2014 for roughly 820 million dollars. B2B outsourcing with little consumer visibility. Stream served clients in more than 20 countries.

Aliso Viejo medical device company that markets the mild procedure, a minimally invasive treatment for lumbar spinal stenosis that removes thickened ligament tissue, plus related devices, to spine and pain specialists in the US. Revenue comes from device sales and procedures reimbursed by Medicare. Private and venture backed. B2B healthcare with no consumer brand. Its mild procedure is performed through a small incision under imaging guidance, avoiding open surgery, which makes it attractive for elderly patients with back pain.

Austin-based luxury vacation rental company that operates smart homes with hotel-style service, sold to travellers through its website and app and marketing in leisure destinations. Revenue comes from nightly bookings. It was founded around 2018 and funded by investors. A consumer travel brand with growing awareness among affluent US travellers. The homes are typically bookable in a few clicks, with in-house cleaning and concierge-style support, and the company positions the product as a hotel alternative for groups and families.

San Carlos, California clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company (Nasdaq: APGN, via a 2022 SPAC) developing sotigalimab, a CD40 antibody for immunotherapy of pancreatic cancer and other tumours. It had no revenue, struggled to fund trials and entered bankruptcy proceedings around 2023-2024. B2B biotech with no consumer profile. Sotigalimab is an antibody designed to activate immune cells and had been tested in combination with chemotherapy. Apexigen had earlier worked with Roche and others.

Philadelphia biotech developing tissue-targeted genetic medicines using Centyrin protein scaffolds, a technology linked to Janssen, to deliver siRNA and other payloads to specific cell types. Privately held and venture funded. Pre-clinical, with partnerships being its route to revenue. B2B only, with no consumer exposure. Centyrins were originally developed as an alternative to antibodies, and Aro is working on gene-silencing and gene-delivery medicines aimed at tissues such as muscle, liver or lungs.

California business software company that provided B2B commerce and sales-configuration applications. Acquired in January 2003 by SEEC Inc. Defunct since. B2B, with no consumer visibility, and now of historical interest only. The product line targeted manufacturers and distributors that needed to quote and sell complex configurable products over the web, and the business shut down long ago. Details of customers and revenue are not documented in the input.

Australia's largest grower and marketer of fresh produce, growing berries, mushrooms, tomatoes, citrus and avocados, with farms across Australia and operations in Morocco and China. It sells mainly to supermarkets such as Woolworths and Coles, with revenue of about 1.4 billion Australian dollars. Formerly ASX-listed (CGC), it was acquired by Paine Schwartz Partners in 2024. Known to supermarket shoppers through its produce labels, but largely B2B.

Pennsylvania clinical-stage biotech (Nasdaq: GRTX) developing avasopasem manganese, a superoxide dismutase mimetic to reduce severe oral mucositis in head and neck cancer patients receiving radiation. The FDA declined approval in 2023 and the company cut costs heavily. B2B biotech, with no consumer profile and no marketed products. Galera was founded in 2012 and listed on Nasdaq in 2019. Radiation mucositis causes painful mouth sores that interrupt cancer treatment, so the market is real, but approval remains a hurdle.

Swedish nanotechnology and display company in Lund developing nanowire-based micro LEDs for displays and lighting, spun out of Lund University research. It licenses its technology and sells products to display makers. Privately held. B2B electronics component developer, with no consumer brand. Glo's microLED approach is intended for smart glasses and wearable screens, where brightness and low power matter. Nanowire LEDs are grown as tiny rods on a chip.

Liqui.do is a business-to-business platform based in Lisbon, Portugal, which according to the input aims to help small and medium-sized enterprises. The input is cut off and does not say which services it provides. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Quebec health and wellness company (Nasdaq: NEPT) that began as a krill oil omega-3 supplier, then moved into consumer packaged goods, buying Sprout Foods, a baby food brand, in 2021, and selling cannabis and wellness products. Boston and Freising, Germany biotechnology company (Nasdaq: PIRS) developing Anticalin proteins, a class of small engineered molecules for cancer and respiratory disease, in collaboration with partners such as Boehringer Ingelheim and Seagen. Indian online and offline securities broker, founded in 1999, offering stock trading, derivatives, mutual funds and wealth products to retail investors through apps, branches and partner networks. Aberdeen-based supplier of specialised lifting, handling and offshore equipment, such as winches, cranes and rental services for the oil and gas industry, as well as technical services and training. Las Vegas e-commerce fulfilment and customer-care company, formerly Navarre, that handled order fulfilment, call-centre work and digital services for consumer brands and retailers. Amsterdam gene therapy company developing vectorised antibodies, using AAV vectors to deliver antibody genes to the brain and central nervous system for diseases such as ALS and Alzheimer's disease. Boston-area biotech developing gildeuretinol, a deuterated vitamin A analogue, to slow vision loss in Stargardt disease and dry age-related macular degeneration. Virginia analytics software company whose 'test and learn' platform helped retailers, restaurants and banks run controlled experiments to find which store formats, promotions or pricing changes drive profit, serving clients such as Starbucks and Walmart. New Jersey medical company (Nasdaq: BLPH) developing INOpulse, a portable inhaled nitric oxide system for patients with pulmonary hypertension linked to lung disease. San Mateo web analytics and digital marketing optimisation company that supplied on-demand analytics to online retailers and brands, helping track visitor behaviour and personalise campaigns. Huisheng Biopharmaceutical is a Beijing-based Chinese biopharma company, described in the input as providing diabetes and complication treatment solutions. Product list, ownership and scale are not given. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Chicago advertising intelligence company, descended from Competitive Media Reporting, that tracks retail ad spending, circulars and digital competitive pricing for retailers, brands and agencies. Offshore business process outsourcing company that ran customer service and back-office centres in the Philippines for US clients. Online job search engine and aggregator, formerly Neuvoo, that collects millions of postings from employers and job boards across more than 70 countries and charges employers on a pay-per-click basis. Mumbai-based Indian manufacturer of polyester products, including PET chips, polyester yarn and films, with plants in India and overseas, such as the Oman and UAE sites. Israeli clinical-stage company (NYSE American: PHGE) developing bacteriophage therapies, viruses that kill specific bacteria, to treat chronic infections in cystic fibrosis and diabetic foot osteomyelitis, with products such as BX004 and BX211. It runs trials in Israel and the US.

Brazilian agricultural inputs retailer and distributor selling seeds, crop protection, fertiliser and technical advice to farmers, and a large footprint of stores in several states. CHINAHRD is a Chinese consulting and human resources company based in Beijing, listed according to the input. The record does not say more about its services or scale. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Jersey-domiciled investment company listed on the London Stock Exchange (3IN) that invests in infrastructure, managed by 3i. Cambridge-based synthetic DNA manufacturer, listed on AIM and the Frankfurt exchange, using enzymatic processes to produce high-fidelity DNA at large scale for use in mRNA and gene therapy production. San Diego clinical-stage biotech (Nasdaq: AARD) developing ARD-101, an oral gut-restricted bitter taste receptor agonist for hyperphagia in Prader-Willi syndrome, with a metabolic disease platform. South Korean biotech listed on KOSDAQ, building bispecific antibodies using its Grabody platform, including programmes for cancer and brain disease. Italian synthetic fibre group listed in Milan, a leader in Econyl regenerated nylon made from fishing nets and waste carpets, and in nylon yarn for carpets and apparel. B2B ingredient brand with fashion industry recognition.

Baoji Pharmaceutical is a Chinese biopharma and biotechnology company with Shanghai listed as its location, according to the input. No product detail or ownership data is available. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

California dental laser company that developed the Waterlase laser systems and diode lasers for dentists, sold in North America, Europe and Asia, with consumables and service revenue. Its lasers are used for hard and soft tissue procedures and aim to reduce pain, drilling and anaesthesia. Biolase was founded in 1987 and grew through dental distributors such as Henry Schein.

Australian neuroscience biotech listed on the ASX and later Nasdaq (BNOX), developing BNC210, a drug for social anxiety disorder and PTSD.
