Bionomics was founded in Adelaide in 1996 and has reorganised its trials through a US Nasdaq listing.

Belgian clinical-stage biotech developing arsenic trioxide-based therapies for autoimmune and inflammatory conditions such as graft versus host disease and systemic sclerosis. Listed on Euronext Brussels and Paris. Pre-revenue and B2B, with no consumer profile. BioSenic's lead product ATO is being tested for chronic graft-versus-host disease, a serious complication of stem cell transplants, and the company is a small Walloon biotech whose shares trade in Brussels and Paris.

Philadelphia clinical-stage biotech (Nasdaq: CNTX) developing hormone-targeted therapies for women's cancers such as breast cancer, including a progesterone receptor antagonist (onapristone) and a bispecific antibody for solid tumours. Pre-revenue, funded by equity. B2B only, no consumer profile. The company was founded in 2015 and went public in 2021. Its strategy of targeting progesterone receptors in breast and other cancers differs from the common use of oestrogen blockers.

Georgia medical device company (Nasdaq: FEMY) selling FemaSeed, a device for intratubal insemination for infertility, FemVue for checking fallopian tube patency, and developing FemBloc, a non-surgical permanent birth control. Customers are fertility clinics and gynaecologists. Revenue is small. B2B, with limited consumer awareness. Femasys was founded in 2004 and listed on Nasdaq in 2021. The potential product, FemBloc, is designed to be an in-office alternative to surgical tubal ligation, which is a large market.

Berlin-founded mobile advertising technology company known for its monetisation platform for app developers, a unit of Digital Turbine since the 2021 acquisition. Customers are app publishers and advertisers. B2B ad tech, with no consumer visibility. Fyber's ad exchange and mediation tools connect app developers with advertisers, and the deal brought the Berlin team into Digital Turbine's mobile app delivery and advertising business.

Israeli clinical-stage pharma (Nasdaq: GLMD) developing aramchol, an oral drug for fatty liver disease and fibrosis (NASH/MASH). A Phase 3 programme did not meet its main goal, after which it looked for alternatives. No product revenue. B2B and no consumer visibility. Galmed is based in Tel Aviv, listed on Nasdaq in 2014 and has a small team. Fatty liver disease affects a very large number of people, and no drug of its kind is widely approved.

Georgia biotech (Nasdaq: GOVX) developing vaccines and immunotherapies using its MVA-VLP platform for COVID-19, mpox and cancer, with a government-funded programme. Revenue is small, from grants and contracts. B2B only and little public awareness. GeoVax's MVA-based vaccine has been supported by US government funding. The company has been in a long period of development, with clinical trials of the cancer therapy and vaccines yet to deliver approvals.

French orthopaedic implant company that developed the Jazz system, a spinal fixation system using flexible bands, and instruments, sold to surgeons and hospitals. Listed on Euronext Growth in Paris and later had financial trouble and restructured. B2B medical devices, with no consumer awareness. Implanet, based near Bordeaux, derived most revenue from the sale of Jazz products and also had a US subsidiary, but it was small and shared a market with large implant companies.

Shanghai biopharmaceutical company developing and producing peptide drugs, including GLP-1 diabetes and obesity medicines, selling to hospitals in China and licensing candidates. Listed. B2B pharma, and low brand awareness outside the industry. Innogen aims at the large Chinese diabetes market, where GLP-1 drugs are in rapid growth. It sells to Chinese hospitals and is relatively new compared to large peers.

Seoul digital marketing and app marketing agency, listed on KOSDAQ, that runs performance advertising campaigns, data tools and influencer work for mobile app and e-commerce clients in Korea and abroad. Revenue comes from ad spending on behalf of customers. B2B, with a modest public profile. MADUP has operated since the 2000s and has been known as a performance marketing agency for Korean mobile games and apps, later adding AI and data products.

New York marketing and advertising holding company (Nasdaq: MDCA), with agencies such as Anomaly, 72andSunny, Doner and Crispin Porter Bogusky in its network, offering creative, digital and media services to big global brands. It merged with Stagwell in 2021. Revenue was around 1.2 billion dollars. B2B agency group, with well-known creative shops but little consumer brand. MDC Partners was founded in 1980 in Toronto, then moved to New York. Customers include consumer, technology and automotive brands. After the merger it was absorbed into the Stagwell group.

Gaithersburg clinical-stage biotech (Nasdaq: NEXI) developing T cell therapies for cancer and autoimmune disease using its AIM nanoparticle platform. It struggled to fund trials and wound down around 2023-2024. B2B and no consumer profile. NexImmune was started with technology from Johns Hopkins and tried to make artificial antigen-presenting cells to direct T cells towards tumours and autoimmune targets. Its stock fell sharply.

Israeli clinical-stage oncology company (Nasdaq: PPBT) developing CM-24, an anti-CEACAM1 antibody, and NT219, a drug aimed at overcoming cancer drug resistance. Pre-revenue with no marketed products. B2B only, and little public awareness. Purple Biotech was formerly named Kitov Pharma and is based in Tel Aviv, with research in Israel, and it receives its funding mostly through Nasdaq share sales and has limited cash.

San Diego clinical-stage biotech (Nasdaq: SKYE) developing nimacimab, a CB1 antibody for obesity, from a cannabinoid-based research history. Pre-revenue and funded by equity. B2B only, no consumer profile. Skye was formerly named Emerald Bioscience and has shifted focus several times, from cannabinoid ideas to metabolic disease. The nimacimab approach is meant to block the CB1 receptor in peripheral tissues and so help with weight loss in conjunction with GLP-1 drugs.

Swedish biotech listed on Nasdaq Stockholm, developing C21 (buloxibutid), an angiotensin II type 2 receptor agonist for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and other lung disease. Pre-revenue, with licensing options. B2B only and no consumer visibility. Vicore is a Swedish company, with C21 in a Phase 2 trial in IPF, and it also worked on a programme for COVID-19 lung disease earlier.

Virginia biotech (Nasdaq: ADTX) that sells AditxtScore immune monitoring tests to labs and health systems and develops Aditxt immune reprogramming therapies for autoimmune conditions and transplant rejection. It acquired and incubated several small ventures, and its revenue is very small compared with its losses. It sells to hospitals, labs and research partners, and has no consumer-facing business, making it a low-profile micro-cap that raises capital frequently through share sales.

Houston clinical-stage oncology company (Nasdaq: BPTH) that developed liposomal antisense drugs, notably prexigebersen (BP1001) for acute myeloid leukaemia and other blood cancers, built on technology licensed from MD Anderson Cancer Center. It has no marketed products and is funded by equity placements, with a small team. B2B drug developer, no consumer profile, and its trials have progressed slowly because of limited capital.

Israeli medical device company, with a US base in Burlington, Massachusetts, that makes the Deep TMS system, a non-invasive magnetic stimulation helmet cleared by the FDA for major depression, obsessive-compulsive disorder and smoking cessation. It sells or leases systems to psychiatric clinics and hospitals and earns recurring treatment fees. Listed on Nasdaq (BWAY) and the Tel Aviv exchange, with revenue of roughly 40 to 50 million dollars. Known mostly to psychiatrists, with growing patient awareness.

Swedish clinical-stage biotech, listed on Nasdaq First North in Stockholm and based in Gothenburg, developing CS1 (valproic acid) for pulmonary arterial hypertension and thrombosis-related diseases, aiming to treat disease through epigenetic effects rather than blood-thinning. EJAM Group is a Guangzhou, China advertising and brand marketing company, listed according to the input. The record does not give its clients, services or revenue. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Maryland regenerative medicine and device company (Nasdaq: ELUT), formerly Aziyo Biologics, that makes biologic envelopes, such as CanGaroo, to hold cardiac implantable devices like pacemakers and reduce infection risk, plus the EluPro antibacterial envelope and orthopaedic and soft tissue products. Customers are hospitals and device manufacturers, and revenue is in the tens of millions of dollars. B2B med-tech, with no consumer recognition.

Danish biotech from Hørsholm, listed on Nasdaq First North in Copenhagen, that uses its ExpreS2 insect-cell protein expression platform to make complex vaccine antigens, with malaria and COVID-19 vaccine projects and a partnership model with research groups and vaccine developers. South Korean biotech listed on KOSDAQ, working on antiviral and anti-cancer candidates built around niclosamide-based drugs and other repurposed compounds, with trials in Korea and abroad. It operates from Seoul and sits among a large group of Korean small-cap biotechs, with trials in oncology and respiratory diseases and a modest scale of operations.

South Korean immuno-oncology biotech based in Gyeonggi province developing antibody-based and cell therapies for cancer and immune diseases, listed on the KOSDAQ market. Revenue comes mainly from licensing and research contracts, and it has no marketed product. B2B biotech with minimal consumer awareness. Its development programmes sit in the antibody and cell therapy area, and it conducts research in Suwon, a city with a strong biotech and electronics cluster. Customers would be pharmaceutical partners buying licences, and hospitals if products are approved.

Sydney-based immunotherapy company, listed on the ASX and Nasdaq (IMMP), developing eftilagimod alpha, a soluble LAG-3 protein that activates antigen-presenting cells, in combination with Merck's Keytruda for lung and head and neck cancer, with partners including Merck, Merck KGaA and Pfizer, and licence revenue from GSK. Pre-commercial with no product sales. B2B with no consumer profile. Immutep is led from Sydney and runs trials in Europe and the US.

Icelandic-Norwegian salmon farming company with operations in the Eastern Fjords of Iceland, based in Eskifjörður, that raises Atlantic salmon in sea cages and also has onshore processing plans. It sells fresh salmon to Europe and North America through seafood distributors. Listed on Euronext Growth Oslo. B2B food producer, with no consumer brand and limited public awareness. Kaldvik's farming sites sit in Iceland's cold, clean fjords, which suits salmon.

La Jolla biopharma (Nasdaq: LBPH) developing bexicaserin, a 5-HT2C agonist for developmental and epileptic encephalopathies such as Dravet syndrome. Danish drugmaker Lundbeck acquired Longboard in late 2024 for about 2.6 billion dollars. Clinical-stage with no revenue and no consumer profile, aimed at neurologists treating rare childhood epilepsies. Dravet syndrome is a rare, severe childhood epilepsy, and the company's candidate is designed to avoid heart valve risks seen in older drugs. Lundbeck's purchase brought a late-stage neurology asset into its portfolio.

Virginia fibre-optic sensing company (Nasdaq: LUNA) selling ODiSI sensors that use optical fibre to measure strain and temperature in aerospace, automotive and energy testing, as well as photonics test products and, earlier, government contract research. It had revenue of roughly 100 million dollars before a restatement and delisting problems. B2B technology supplier, with no consumer profile. Luna was founded in 1990 and later sold or reorganised parts of the business.

Micro Communication is a Chinese advertising and digital marketing company based in Beijing, listed according to the input. No details of its clients or channels are available. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Finnish nanotechnology and pharmaceutical engineering company, listed on Nasdaq First North in Helsinki, that uses its CESS supercritical fluid technology to shrink poorly soluble drug molecules into nanoparticles that dissolve better. Customers are pharma firms paying for development projects and sometimes taking licences, and it also advances its own pipeline. B2B drug delivery specialist, with no consumer profile. Nanoform was founded in 2015 and spun out of research at the University of Helsinki.

Maryland cell and gene therapy company (Nasdaq: ORGS) built around its point-of-care model, in which therapies are made near the patient, with a development and manufacturing network of hospital partners in the US, Europe and Asia and a regenerative medicine licensing business. Revenue is small and has come from contract manufacturing and licensing. B2B only, with limited public awareness. Orgenesis is headquartered in Germantown, Maryland, and operates internationally.

Canadian cannabis company, formerly CannaRoyalty, that held licensed producer and brand interests in California, including the Lowell and Cypress brands, and operated cultivation and distribution there. Cannabis B2B and brand operator, with some consumer brands in California.

UK property investment company in Potters Bar, listed on AIM, owning a portfolio of shops, offices and other commercial properties, mainly in London and the South East, and earning rental income from commercial tenants and also holding a portfolio of shares. Controlled by long-time directors. Small and conservative, with no consumer profile. It has been listed for decades and its stock is thinly traded.

South Korean biopharma developing diagnostics and treatments for neurodegenerative disease and other conditions, listed on KOSDAQ and based in Seongnam. PeopleBio is a small Korean developer in the Seongnam area, close to Pangyo, the country's technology and biotech cluster. It is an early-stage company, and any product revenue would come mainly from diagnostics and hospital customers.

French industrial 3D printing group, part of the Gorgé family-controlled group, offering 3D printers, materials, and printed parts and products, including dental products, to industry and healthcare. Listed on Euronext Paris, it has subsidiaries in France and elsewhere. B2B manufacturer with no consumer brand. The group manufactures industrial 3D printers, resin and powder materials, and produces parts for aerospace, medical and consumer products. It is a mid-sized specialist with annual revenue in the tens of millions of euros.

Redwood City advertising technology company (Nasdaq: PUBM) running a sell-side platform that lets publishers such as news sites, app developers and streaming services sell ad space to advertisers and agencies through programmatic auctions, with a growing connected TV and mobile video business. Revenue is about 280 million dollars. Founded 2006. B2B with no consumer visibility. Customers include publishers and platforms, and the company competes with Google and Magnite.

Texas wound care and surgical products company (Nasdaq: SMTI) selling CellerateRX, BIAKOS antimicrobial wound products and other advanced wound care items, to physicians, hospitals and surgical centres. Revenue is about 70 to 100 million dollars. B2B healthcare supplier with no consumer brand. Sanara MedTech has grown through acquisitions and licensing, and relies on a specialist sales force that visits wound clinics, nursing facilities and surgeons. Its products are mainly reimbursed through hospital and clinic purchases.

Scientop is a Changsha, Hunan, China company that, according to the input, makes hardware for industrial automation, and it is listed. No product details are available. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

North Carolina biotech contract manufacturer (Nasdaq: SCPX), formerly NightHawk Biosciences, which bought the former Heat Biologics business and operates a CDMO for biologics and viral vectors from a plant in San Antonio, Texas. It sells manufacturing services to biotech and pharma customers. B2B with no consumer profile. Scorpius also provides analytical and fill-finish capabilities and serves clients that need clinical-stage manufacturing of biologic drugs.

California public safety technology company (Nasdaq: SSTI), formerly ShotSpotter, whose acoustic sensors and software detect and locate gunfire for police departments in more than 160 US cities. It also sells ResourceRouter, CrimeTracer and Safepointe. Customers are municipal governments, and revenue is about 90 million dollars. B2B and government sales, with controversy over accuracy. SoundThinking is based in the Bay Area and was founded in 1996 as SST.

Austin biotech (Nasdaq: TFFP) developing inhaled dry powder drugs using its Thin Film Freezing technology, including vaccines and antivirals, with partnerships with universities and drug makers. Revenue is minimal. B2B drug delivery developer, with no consumer visibility. Its Thin Film Freezing creates powders that can be inhaled, for example against lung infections. TFF also tests its approach with partners such as the University of Texas. The company has had no product launches.

California late-stage pharma (Nasdaq: UNCY) developing oxylanthanum carbonate, a phosphate binder for hyperphosphatemia in patients with chronic kidney disease on dialysis, aimed at a market dominated by Sanofi's Renvela and others. Pre-revenue. B2B, selling to nephrologists and dialysis operators in future. No consumer profile. Unicycive was founded in 2016 and reports to investors from California. The company has faced FDA manufacturing issues for its lead product.

Rochester, New York clinical-stage biotech (Nasdaq: VCNX) developing pepinemab, an antibody against semaphorin 4D, in Huntington's disease, Alzheimer's disease and cancer, with a partnership with Merck KGaA. Pre-revenue. B2B and no consumer profile. Vaccinex was founded in 2001 and went public in 2018. Its antibody pepinemab was tested in Huntington's disease and showed some signals, but regulatory progress needs more data.

Guangzhou mobile advertising platform, known as Youmi, that ran an app promotion and ad network for Android and iOS developers, serving app makers and advertisers in China. Revenue comes from advertising spend. B2B, with little consumer recognition. Youmi was founded in the early 2010s and is based in the South China tech hub of Guangzhou. Its advertising unit competed with larger Chinese platforms such as Baidu and Tencent.

French biotech listed on Euronext Paris developing glenzocimab, an antibody that blocks platelet glycoprotein VI to treat acute ischaemic stroke without increasing bleeding risk. Pre-revenue, with trials in Europe. B2B and no consumer profile. Acticor was founded in 2013 as a spin-out from French research institutes and its drug is designed to be given in ambulances or at hospital admission. Stroke is a major cause of death and disability, so a safe clot treatment would be significant.

Atlanta biotech (NYSE American: ALZN) developing lithium-based AL001 for Alzheimer's disease and a vaccine for the same disease, licensed from the University of South Florida. Pre-revenue. B2B and no consumer profile. Alzamend is based in Atlanta, with a small team, and it lists on the NYSE American. Its lithium formulation aims to reduce the side effects of older lithium treatments. It also works on a vaccine for Alzheimer's.

Applied UV was a manufacturer of ultraviolet disinfection systems under the SteriLumen brand and of hospitality furniture through MunnWorks, selling to hospitals, schools and hotels. Listed on Nasdaq (AUVI), it struggled financially and filed for bankruptcy in 2024. Defunct B2B company with no consumer brand. Its UV disinfection range was marketed for hospitals, schools and hotels during COVID-19 and shrank afterwards.

Danish biotech from Kongens Lyngby that makes Aquaporin Inside membranes, which use biomimetic water channel proteins to filter water for desalination, industrial reuse and space applications. Customers are industrial and water treatment firms. Listed on Nasdaq First North, with a small revenue. B2B and not a consumer brand. The company was founded in 2005 and is based in Kongens Lyngby near Copenhagen, working with water research teams in Denmark and Singapore.

Puerto Rico-based biopharma that listed on Nasdaq (ASBP) in 2025 and is developing sublingual and intravenous aspirin formulations aimed at faster onset for heart attack and pain.
